report_sentences: # Gravity with a Colour–Temperature Coupling, plus Shape-Dependent Quadratic Drag, in a Simulated Ballistics Laboratory
Gravity is not constant: it depends on an interaction between reflectance and temperature, g = g₀[1 + c(R − R₀)(T − T₀)], with g₀ ≈ 9.80 m/s², c ≈ 1.0×10⁻³ °C⁻¹, R₀ ≈ 0.48 and T₀ ≈ 21 °C.
- Extreme-value combinations of reflectance, temperature, stripes, hardness and batch, on a high-drag cube.
- A 3×3 grid of reflectance × temperature for the cube in air.
These covered reflectance values {0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1} and temperatures {−20, 5, 30, 55, 80} °C, plus vacuum throws.
- With other properties held fixed, a black object (R = 0) falls faster when cold.
- Grey objects (R = 0.5) show essentially no temperature dependence.
- Neither reflectance nor temperature has a main effect when the other variable sits at its neutral value.
Hot dark objects and cold light objects are "lighter" (smaller g); cold dark objects and hot light objects are "heavier" (larger g).
irrelevant_property_sentences: Stripes, hardness and batch had no detectable effect.
- Extreme-value combinations of reflectance, temperature, stripes, hardness and batch, on a high-drag cube.
- In the residual regressions, stripes, hardness and batch were not significant (all p > 0.25).
This applies, for example, to weak effects of stripes or hardness, or to small shape-specific corrections.
